romaji: Natsu ni naru to, Nihon de omatsuri ga takusan arimasu ne.
english: When summer comes, there are many festivals in Japan, aren't there?
exampleRomaji: Natsu ni naru to, Nihon de omatsuri ga takusan arimasu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 夏(なつ)になると、日(に)本(ほん)でお祭(まつ)りがたくさんありますね。
exampleEn: When summer comes, there are many festivals in Japan, aren't there?
audioPath: clips/001_夏になると、日本でお祭りがたくさんありますね。.wav
grammar2:
辞(じ)書(しょ)形(けい) + と = when (natural consequence)
夏(なつ) (summer) ↔ 冬(ふゆ) (winter)

exampleRomaji: Hai.
japaneseFurigana: はい。
exampleEn: Yes.
audioPath: clips/002_はい。.wav

romaji: Omatsuri wa jinja no kamisama no tame no ibento desu.
english: Festivals are events held for the gods at shrines.
exampleRomaji: Omatsuri wa jinja no kamisama no tame no ibento desu.
japaneseFurigana: お祭(まつ)りは神社(じんじゃ)の神(かみ)様(さま)のためのイベントです。
exampleEn: Festivals are events held for the gods at shrines.
audioPath: clips/003_お祭りは神社の神様のためのイベントです。.wav
grammar2:
名(めい)詞(し) + のため = for the sake of / for
神(かみ)様(さま) = god

romaji: Kamisama no tame no omatsuri desu ka?
english: Are festivals held for the gods?
exampleRomaji: Kamisama no tame no omatsuri desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 神(かみ)様(さま)のためのお祭(まつ)りですか？
exampleEn: Are festivals held for the gods?
audioPath: clips/004_神様のためのお祭りですか.wav
grammar2: 名(めい)詞(し) + のため = for the sake of / for

exampleRomaji: Sou desu.
japaneseFurigana: そうです。
exampleEn: That's right.
audioPath: clips/005_そうです。.wav

romaji: Kamisama ni kansha suru tame ni omatsuri o shimasu.
english: We hold festivals to express our gratitude to the gods.
exampleRomaji: Kamisama ni kansha suru tame ni omatsuri o shimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 神(かみ)様(さま)に感(かん)謝(しゃ)するために、お祭(まつ)りをします。
exampleEn: We hold festivals to express our gratitude to the gods.
audioPath: clips/006_神様に感謝するためにお祭りをします。.wav
grammar2:
辞(じ)書(しょ)形(けい) + ために = in order to
感(かん)謝(しゃ)する = to thank / appreciate

romaji: Omatsuri de minna ga omoi hako o katsuide imasu ne.
english: During the festival, everyone is carrying the heavy box, aren't they?
exampleRomaji: Omatsuri de minna ga omikoshi o katsuide imasu ne.
japaneseFurigana: お祭(まつ)りでみんながお神(み)輿(こし)をかついでいますね。
exampleEn: During the festival, everyone is carrying the portable shrine, aren't they?
audioPath: clips/007_お祭りでみんなが思い箱をかついでいますね。.wav
grammar2:
重(おも)い (heavy) ↔ 軽(かる)い (light)
担(かつ)ぐ = to carry on one's shoulder

romaji: Are wa omikoshi to iimasu.
english: That is called a 'mikoshi' (portable shrine).
exampleRomaji: Are wa omikoshi to iimasu.
japaneseFurigana: あれはお神(み)輿(こし)といいます。
exampleEn: That is called a 'mikoshi' (portable shrine).
audioPath: clips/008_あれはおみこしといいます。.wav
grammar2:
〜と言(い)う = to be called / named
お神(み)輿(こし) = portable shrine

romaji: Kamisama ga noru norimono desu.
english: It is a vehicle for the gods to ride in.
exampleRomaji: Kamisama ga noru norimono desu.
japaneseFurigana: 神(かみ)様(さま)が乗(の)る乗(の)り物(もの)です。
exampleEn: It is a vehicle for the gods to ride in.
audioPath: clips/009_神様が乗る乗り物です。.wav
grammar2:
乗(の)る (to ride) ↔ 降(お)りる (to get off)
乗(の)り物(もの) = vehicle

romaji: Kamisama no kuruma mitai na mono desu ne.
english: It's like a car for the gods, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Kamisama no kuruma mitai na mono desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 神(かみ)様(さま)の車(くるま)みたいなものですね。
exampleEn: It's like a car for the gods, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/010_神様の車みたいなものですね。.wav
grammar2: 〜みたいな = like / similar to

exampleRomaji: Hai.
japaneseFurigana: はい。
exampleEn: Yes.
audioPath: clips/011_はい。.wav

romaji: 'Wasshoi' to iinagara minna de katsugimasu.
english: Everyone shouts 'Wasshoi!' while carrying it together.
exampleRomaji: "Wasshoi" to iinagara minna de katsugimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 「わっしょい」と言(い)いながら皆(みんな)で担(かつ)ぎます。
exampleEn: Everyone shouts 'Wasshoi!' while carrying it together.
audioPath: clips/012_わっしょいと言いながらみんなで担ぎます。.wav
grammar2:
ます形(けい) + ながら = while doing...
わっしょい = Wasshoi (traditional festival chant)

romaji: Doushite yurashinagara arukimasu ka?
english: Why do you walk while shaking it?
exampleRomaji: Dōshite yurashinagara arukimasu ka?
japaneseFurigana: どうして揺(ゆ)らしながら歩(ある)きますか？
exampleEn: Why do you walk while shaking it?
audioPath: clips/013_どうして揺らしながら歩きますか.wav
grammar2:
ます形(けい) + ながら = while doing...
歩(ある)く (to walk) ↔ 走(はし)る (to run)

romaji: Omikoshi o yurasu to kamisama ga yorokobimasu.
english: The gods are pleased when the mikoshi (portable shrine) is shaken.
exampleRomaji: Omikoshi o yurasu to kamisama ga yorokobimasu.
japaneseFurigana: おみこしを揺(ゆ)らすと神(かみ)様(さま)が喜(よろこ)びます。
exampleEn: The gods are pleased when the mikoshi (portable shrine) is shaken.
audioPath: clips/014_おみこしを揺らすと神様が喜びます。.wav
grammar2:
辞(じ)書(しょ)形(けい) + と = when / if
喜(よろこ)ぶ (to be pleased/happy) ↔ 悲(かな)しむ (to be sad)

romaji: Kamisama ga yorokobu to machi ga genki ni narimasu ka?
english: Does the town become lively when the gods are pleased?
exampleRomaji: Kamisama ga yorokobu to machi ga genki ni narimasu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 神(かみ)様(さま)が喜(よろこ)ぶと町(まち)が元(げん)気(き)になりますか？
exampleEn: Does the town become lively when the gods are pleased?
audioPath: clips/015_神様が喜ぶと町が元気になりますか.wav
grammar2:
〜になる = to become
元(げん)気(き) (healthy/lively) ↔ 病(びょう)気(き) (sick)

exampleRomaji: Sō desu.
japaneseFurigana: そうです。
exampleEn: That's right.
audioPath: clips/016_そうです。.wav

romaji: Byouki ga nakunattari, okome ga takusan toretari shimasu.
english: People may recover from illnesses, and the town may have a good rice harvest.
exampleRomaji: Byōki ga nakunattari, kome ga takusan toretari shimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 病(びょう)気(き)が無(な)くなったり、米(こめ)がたくさん取(と)れたりします。
exampleEn: People may recover from illnesses, and the town may have a good rice harvest.
audioPath: clips/017_病気がなくなったり、お米がたくさん取れたりします。.wav
grammar2:
〜たり〜たりする = do things like...
なくなる = to disappear / go away

romaji: Omikoshi wa dare demo katsugu koto ga dekimasu ka?
english: Can anyone carry the mikoshi?
exampleRomaji: Omikoshi wa dare demo katsugu koto ga dekimasu ka?
japaneseFurigana: おみこしは誰(だれ)でも担(かつ)ぐことができますか？
exampleEn: Can anyone carry the mikoshi?
audioPath: clips/018_おみこしは誰でも担ぐことができますか.wav
grammar2:
疑(ぎ)問(もん)詞(し) + でも = anyone / anything / anywhere
辞(じ)書(しょ)形(けい) + ことができる = can do

romaji: Tokubetsu na fuku o kita hito ga katsugimasu.
english: Only people wearing special clothing carry it.
exampleRomaji: Tokubetsu na fuku o kita hito ga katsugimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 特(とく)別(べつ)な服(ふく)を着(き)た人(ひと)が担(かつ)ぎます。
exampleEn: Only people wearing special clothing carry it.
audioPath: clips/019_特別な服を着た人が担ぎます。.wav
grammar2:
特(とく)別(べつ)な = special
着(き)る (to wear - upper body) ↔ 脱(ぬ)ぐ (to take off clothes)

romaji: Happi to iimasu.
english: It is called a 'happi' coat.
exampleRomaji: Happi to iimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 法(はっ)便(ぴ)といいます。
exampleEn: It is called a 'happi' coat.
audioPath: clips/020_ハッピと言います。.wav
grammar2:
〜と言(い)う = to be called / named
法(はっ)被(ぴ) = Happi coat (traditional festival coat)

romaji: Karafuru na fuku desu ne.
english: Your clothes are so colorful, aren't they?
exampleRomaji: Karafuru na fuku desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: カラフルな服(ふく)ですね。
exampleEn: Your clothes are so colorful, aren't they?
audioPath: clips/021_カラフルな服ですね。.wav
grammar2: カラフルな = colorful

romaji: Kakkoii desu.
english: That looks cool.
exampleRomaji: Kakkoii desu.
japaneseFurigana: かっこいいです。
exampleEn: That looks cool.
audioPath: clips/022_かっこいいです。.wav
grammar2: かっこいい (cool/attractive) ↔ かっこ悪(わる)い (uncool)

romaji: Omatsuri no yoru wa takusan no yatai ga demasu.
english: On the night of the festival, many food stalls come out.
exampleRomaji: O-matsuri no yoru wa takusan no yatai ga demasu.
japaneseFurigana: お祭(まつ)りの夜(よる)は、たくさんの屋(や)台(だい)が出(で)ます。
exampleEn: On the night of the festival, many food stalls come out.
audioPath: clips/023_お祭りの夜はたくさんの屋台が出ます。.wav
grammar2:
夜(よる) (night) ↔ 昼(ひる) (daytime)
屋(や)台(だい) = food stall / booth

romaji: Yatai de wa oishii tabemono ga utteimasu ne.
english: At the food stalls, they sell delicious food, don't they?
exampleRomaji: Yatai de wa oishii tabemono ga utteimasu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 屋(や)台(だい)では美(おい)味(み)しい食(た)べ物(もの)が売(う)っていますね。
exampleEn: At the food stalls, they sell delicious food, don't they?
audioPath: clips/024_屋台では美味しい食べ物が売っていますね。.wav
grammar2:
美(おい)味(しい) (delicious) ↔ まずい (bad tasting)
売(う)る (to sell) ↔ 買(か)う (to buy)

romaji: Yakisoba ya takoyaki ya kakigouri ga arimasu.
english: There are yakisoba, takoyaki, and shaved ice.
exampleRomaji: Yakisoba ya takoyaki, kakigōri ga arimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 焼(や)きそばや、たこ焼(や)きや、かき氷(ごおり)があります。
exampleEn: There are yakisoba, takoyaki, and shaved ice.
audioPath: clips/025_焼きそばやたこ焼きやかき氷があります。.wav
grammar2:
〜や〜や = and... and... (non-exhaustive list)
たこ焼(や)き = takoyaki (octopus balls)

romaji: Watashi wa takoyaki ga ichiban suki desu.
english: I like takoyaki the best.
exampleRomaji: Watashi wa takoyaki ga ichiban suki desu.
japaneseFurigana: 私(わたし)はたこ焼(や)きが一(いち)番(ばん)好(す)きです。
exampleEn: I like takoyaki the best.
audioPath: clips/026_私はたこ焼きが一番好きです。.wav
grammar2:
一(いち)番(ばん) + 形(けい)容(よう)詞(し) = the most...
好(す)き (like) ↔ 嫌(きら)い (dislike)

romaji: Watashi wa omatsuri no geemu ga suki desu.
english: I like the games at the festival.
exampleRomaji: Watashi wa o-matsuri no gēmu ga suki desu.
japaneseFurigana: 私(わたし)はお祭(まつ)りのゲームが好(す)きです。
exampleEn: I like the games at the festival.
audioPath: clips/027_私はお祭りのゲームが好きです。.wav
grammar2: 名(めい)詞(し) + が好(す)きです = to like something

romaji: Kingyo sukui ga arimasu.
english: There is a goldfish scooping game.
exampleRomaji: Kingyo sukui ga arimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 金(きん)魚(ぎょ)すくいがあります。
exampleEn: There is a goldfish scooping game.
audioPath: clips/028_金魚すくいがあります。.wav
grammar2: 金(きん)魚(ぎょ)すくい = goldfish scooping (traditional festival game)

romaji: Chiisai sakana o ami de sukuu geemu desu ne.
english: It's a game where you scoop up small fish with a net, right?
exampleRomaji: Chiisai sakana o ami de sukuu gēmu desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 小(ちい)さい魚(さかな)を網(あみ)ですくうゲームですね。
exampleEn: It's a game where you scoop up small fish with a net, right?
audioPath: clips/029_小さい魚を網ですくうゲームですね。.wav
grammar2:
小(ちい)さい (small) ↔ 大(おお)きい (large)
すくう = to scoop up

romaji: Hai, kodomo-tachi ni totemo ninki ga arimasu.
english: Yes, it is very popular among children.
exampleRomaji: Hai, kodomo-tachi ni totemo ninki ga arimasu.
japaneseFurigana: はい、子(こ)どもたちにとても人(にん)気(き)があります。
exampleEn: Yes, it is very popular among children.
audioPath: clips/030_はい、子供たちにとても人気があります。.wav
grammar2:
人(にん)気(き)がある = to be popular
子(こ)ども (child) ↔ 大(おと)な (adult)

romaji: Taiko no oto mo kikoemasu ne.
english: You can hear the sound of the taiko drums, can't you?
exampleRomaji: Taiko no oto mo kikoemasu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 太(たい)鼓(こ)の音(おと)も聞(き)こえますね。
exampleEn: You can hear the sound of the taiko drums, can't you?
audioPath: clips/031_太鼓の音も聞こえますね。.wav
grammar2:
聞(き)こえる = to be audible / can hear
太(たい)鼓(こ) = Taiko drum (traditional Japanese drum)

romaji: Are wa bonodori no ongaku desu.
english: That is the music for Bon Odori (a traditional Japanese dance festival).
exampleRomaji: Are wa, bonodori no ongaku desu.
japaneseFurigana: あれは、盆(ぼん)踊(おど)りの音(おん)楽(がく)です。
exampleEn: That is the music for Bon Odori (a traditional Japanese dance festival).
audioPath: clips/032_あれは、盆踊りの音楽です。.wav
grammar2: 盆(ぼん)踊(おど)り = Bon Odori (traditional summer dance)

romaji: Minna de wa ni natte odorimasu.
english: Everyone forms a circle and dances together.
exampleRomaji: Minna de wa ni natte odorimasu.
japaneseFurigana: みんなで輪(わ)になって踊(おど)ります。
exampleEn: Everyone forms a circle and dances together.
audioPath: clips/033_みんなで縁になって踊ります。.wav
grammar2:
輪(わ)になる = to form a circle
踊(おど)る = to dance

romaji: Gaikokujin mo issho ni odottemo ii desu ka?
english: Is it okay for foreigners to dance together as well?
exampleRomaji: Gaikokujin mo issho ni odottemo ii desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 外(がい)国(こく)人(じん)も一(いっ)緒(しょ)に踊(おど)ってもいいですか？
exampleEn: Is it okay for foreigners to dance together as well?
audioPath: clips/034_外国人も一緒に踊ってもいいですか.wav
grammar2:
て形(けい) + もいいですか = May I do...?
外(がい)国(こく)人(じん) (foreigner) ↔ 日(に)本(ほん)人(じん) (Japanese person)

exampleRomaji: Mochiron desu.
japaneseFurigana: もちろんです。
exampleEn: Of course, it is.
audioPath: clips/035_もちろんです。.wav

romaji: Issho ni odoru to tanoshii desu yo.
english: It's fun to dance together.
exampleRomaji: Issho ni odoru to tanoshii desu yo.
japaneseFurigana: 一(いっ)緒(しょ)に踊(おど)ると楽(たの)しいですよ。
exampleEn: It's fun to dance together.
audioPath: clips/036_一食に踊ると楽しいですよ。.wav
grammar2:
辞(じ)書(しょ)形(けい) + と = when / if
楽(たの)しい (fun/enjoyable) ↔ つまらない (boring)

romaji: Koteshi no natsuyasumi wa omatsuri ni ikitai desu.
english: I want to go to a festival during this summer vacation.
exampleRomaji: Kotoshi no natsuyasumi wa omatsuri ni ikitai desu.
japaneseFurigana: 今(こと)年(し)の夏(なつ)休(やす)みはお祭(まつ)りに行(い)きたいです。
exampleEn: I want to go to a festival during this summer vacation.
audioPath: clips/037_今年の夏休みはお祭りに行きたいです。.wav
grammar2:
ます形(けい) + たい = want to do
夏(なつ)休(やす)み = summer vacation

romaji: Chikaku no jinja no sukejuuru o shirabemashou.
english: Let's check the schedule of the nearby shrine.
exampleRomaji: Chikaku no jinja no yotei o shirabemashou.
japaneseFurigana: 近(ちか)くの神(じん)社(じゃ)の予(よ)定(てい)を調(しら)べましょう。
exampleEn: Let's check the schedule of the nearby shrine.
audioPath: clips/038_近くの神社のスケジュールを調べましょう。.wav
grammar2:
ます形(けい) + ましょう = let's do
近(ちか)く (near) ↔ 遠(とお)く (far)

exampleRomaji: Hai, onegaishimasu.
japaneseFurigana: はい、お願(ねが)いします。
exampleEn: Yes, please (do so).
audioPath: clips/039_はい、お願いします。.wav

romaji: Yukata o kite ikitai desu.
english: I want to go wearing a yukata (a casual summer kimono).
exampleRomaji: Yukata o kite ikitai desu.
japaneseFurigana: 浴(ゆ)衣(かた)を着(き)て行(い)きたいです。
exampleEn: I want to go wearing a yukata (a casual summer kimono).
audioPath: clips/040_浴衣を着て行きたいです。.wav
grammar2:
て形(けい) + 行(い)く = go doing something
浴(ゆ)衣(かた) = Yukata (casual summer kimono)

romaji: Yukata wa natsu ni pittari no kimono desu ne.
english: A yukata is the perfect kimono for summer, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Yukata wa natsu ni pittari no kimono desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 浴衣(ゆかた)は夏(なつ)にぴったりの着(き)物(もの)ですね。
exampleEn: A yukata is the perfect kimono for summer, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/041_浴衣は夏にぴったりの着物ですね。.wav
grammar2:
名(めい)詞(し) + にぴったり = perfect match for...
着(き)物(もの) = Kimono (traditional Japanese clothing)

romaji: Shashin o takusan toritai desu.
english: I want to take lots of photos.
exampleRomaji: Shashin o takusan toritai desu.
japaneseFurigana: 写(しゃ)真(しん)をたくさん撮(と)りたいです。
exampleEn: I want to take lots of photos.
audioPath: clips/042_写真をたくさん撮りたいです。.wav
grammar2: 写(しゃ)真(しん)を撮(と)る = to take a photo

romaji: Tanoshii omoide o tsukurimashou.
english: Let's make wonderful memories together.
exampleRomaji: Tanoshii omoide o tsukurimashou.
japaneseFurigana: 楽(たの)しい思(おも)い出(で)を作(つく)りましょう。
exampleEn: Let's make wonderful memories together.
audioPath: clips/043_楽しい思い出を作りましょう。.wav
grammar2:
ます形(けい) + ましょう = let's do
思(おも)い出(で) = memory
